content:
adrian: Heads-up — started seeing OOMs on the continuous-batching path for long-chat workloads. Root seems to be KV cache memory pressure during batch formation (we were summing token budgets, not KV mem). Repro + profile: https://dash.internal/redwood/perf/pprof?id=1760001234 :point_right:

adrian: quick excerpt from CPU/alloc profile:
```
# alloc_objects  alloc_space  stack
1200            98.3MB     runtime/kvcache.(*Shard).Put
880             72.6MB     runtime/kvcache.(*KV).Alloc
... (trimmed)
```

maria: ugh. so batching was admitting requests until token_budget_sum < BATCH_TOKEN_TARGET, right? we never converted tokens -> kv bytes.

adrian: exactly. token_budget target (512 tokens) looked reasonable until you mix in many long histories (chat sessions with 2048+ context). the per-token KV cost multiplies by layers/heads and dtype. we should compute an admission budget in bytes.

kevin: proposing a simple change: each request carries an estimated kv_bytes field computed at enqueue time: `kv_bytes = tokens * kv_bytes_per_token` where `kv_bytes_per_token` = layers * hidden_dim * 2 * 4 bytes * fudge_factor. then batch admission sums kv_bytes + kernel_overhead_estimate and compares against `gpu_free_mem * (1 - kv_memory_safety_margin)`. config snippet:
```yaml
queue_policy: kv-aware
batching:
  token_budget_target: 512
  kv_safety_margin: 0.30  # fraction of GPU mem reserved
  max_batch_kv_bytes: null  # computed per-device
```

maria: tried local A/B with `kv_safety_margin=0.30` and `kv_bytes_per_token=48` (our 7B/16layer quantized profile). results over 1h: OOMs dropped from 23->1, p95 latency went up ~14ms, median up ~6ms. tradeoff seems ok.

perf-bot: telemetry: OOM_count{service="runtime",cluster="eu-west-1"} 23 -> 1 (last 60m). See runbook: https://confluence.redwood/ops/ooms

elaine: are we sure 48 bytes is right across kernels? some kernel implementations allocate extra workspace when batch_size>1 (KV packing, attention workspace). kernel memory overhead needs to be added to the budget.

kevin: good call. added a `kernel_overhead_per_batch_bytes` term measured per model+kernel in the model profile registry. admission then enforces: sum(request.kv_bytes) + kernel_overhead <= free_mem*(1-margin).

adrian: also hit a fairness issue: large requests get starved while many tiny requests fill the batch. suggestion: maintain two sub-queues: interactive (<=64 tokens) and standard. always reserve X% headroom for interactive until burst limit. draft policy:
- admission loop pulls from interactive queue first up to reserved_kv_bytes
- then fills from standard queue constrained by remaining kv budget
- if a single request's kv_bytes > max_batch_kv_bytes: fallback to single-request mode (no batching) or reject with 413-like error

maria: ran sim with 10% interactive reserve, kv_safety_margin=0.35 -> OOMs 0, median latency +8ms, p99 for long requests improved vs previous because we avoid OOM-triggered falls.

kevin: another edge: when we evict/trim KV cache to free memory, that can increase future compute for those sessions. maybe prefer admission-time skipping of high-kv queries instead of evicting active contexts. eviction policy: LRU by last_active_token and bounded per-session.

adrian: agreed. we should prefer throttle/queueing before eviction. also add a preemptive async background compressor which can quantize older KV shards to smaller dtype to reclaim mem (best-effort).

elaine: we need tests:
- unit test: batch admit sums with mocked kernel overheads and rejects correctly
- load test: replay mixed chat traces (we have `replay/traces/long-chat-2025-11.json`) and assert OOMs=0 for 1h bootstrap
- regression test: measure latency delta < 20% for median and p95 < +50ms on 7B baseline

adrian: I'll open a PR with the admission change + config + docs. draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4381 (WIP: batch-kv-safety). notes in PR: we add `estimated_kv_bytes` to `QueuedRequest` and a new `kv_aware_admitter` with two-queue policy.

kevin: small perf note: kernel selection currently picks best throughput kernel for given batch_size. if admission favors smaller batches (to reduce kv mem), we should update kernel-selection cost model to include memory footprint tradeoffs, e.g. prefer kernels that use less workspace when memory tight even if throughput per-token slightly lower. I'll add a flag `prefer_low_mem_kernel` to the scheduler.

maria: outstanding action items:
- adrian: PR + unit tests (#4381)
- kevin: add kernel memory cost to profile registry + switch flag
- elaine: load-test job + add trace to replay suite
- infra: tune `kv_safety_margin` default to 0.30 across hosted clusters, allow overrides per-tenant

adrian: thanks folks. will iterate on PR. ping me if you want to try other `kv_bytes_per_token` constants — I left a small helper `scripts/estimate_kv.py` in the branch to compute per-model values from registry. :rocket:

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0042 for OOM surge (linked to thread). status: monitoring.

kevin: cool, once PR lands I'll run a canary with `kv_safety_margin=0.25` then 0.30 across EU cluster.

maria: 👍 good work.
